summary:
G3 English review of EFMP-302 Unit 6 (Sustaining Professionalism through Continuous Learning), the final unit of the course.
DISPOSITION: escalate. Two of the seven required criteria fail on observed defects (assessment, accessibility), one is unverified because the bundle binds no source text (sources), and four pass (authority, coverage, readability, pedagogy).

Escalation grounds, distinct from the ordinary revise loop:
1. MISSING EVIDENCE. The prepared bundle binds 107 inputs and not one of them is the text, abstract or record of any of the six cited works. Citation existence was all that could be checked, so source support is undecidable at this gate. A new bundle binding the cited passages is required before 'sources' can be decided either way.
2. OUT-OF-UNIT REPAIR. The ERQ rubric tables are clipped and unreachable at 360px and 414px, with no scroll recovery. The same defect reproduces on EFMP-302 units 02 and 05, so it is a site-wide theme/CSS problem that no edit to Unit 6 prose can fix and that a unit author cannot own.

Revise-class defects the author can repair now: the MCQ 4 key contradicts its own stem and the taught text (keyed 'd', derived 'b'); the RRQ 7 mark scheme pairs an action with a principle the topic never attributes to it; six 'the figure above' references point at figures that do not render because all eight are still prompt-only markers; and the approved blueprint's one-ERQ-per-topic rule and its required 'critique a sample development plan' item are both unmet.

What is genuinely strong: authority tracks cleanly from the course guide's 6.1-6.4 leaf bullets through the approved content-spec to all four topic files; all 13 sub-topics are taught substantively rather than headed; the HSC register holds throughout with every glossed term resolving; the nine-part topic cycle is complete and the activities are feasible and concretely specified for Pakistani government-school conditions; and the unit closes the course deliberately rather than merely ending. Nine of ten MCQ keys match my independent answers.

This report is advisory. It is unsigned, no qualification record or registry entry exists for this reviewer, and nothing here certifies the unit, writes a tracker row or authorises publication.
